name: Common hepatic artery
note: The common hepatic artery is a short blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the liver, pylorus of the stomach, duodenum, pancreas, and gallbladder.

name: Gastroduodenal artery
note: In anatomy, the gastroduodenal artery is a small blood vessel in the abdomen.

name: Proper hepatic artery
note: The hepatic artery proper (also proper hepatic artery) is the artery that supplies the liver and gallbladder.

name: Left gastric artery
note: In human anatomy, the left gastric artery arises from the celiac artery and runs along the superior portion of the lesser curvature of the stomach.

name: Splenic artery
note: The splenic artery or lienal artery is the blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the spleen.

name: Inferior mesenteric artery
note: In human anatomy, the inferior mesenteric artery, often abbreviated as IMA, is the third main branch of the abdominal aorta and arises at the level of L3, supplying the large intestine from the distal transverse colon to the upper part of the anal canal.

name: Left colic artery
note: The left colic artery is a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery.

name: Ascending branch of left colic artery
Descending branch of left colic artery
Sigmoid arteries
note: The sigmoid arteries, two or three in number, run obliquely downward and to the left behind the peritoneum and in front of the psoas major, ureter, and internal spermatic vessels.

name: Inferior phrenic artery
note: The inferior phrenic arteries are two small vessels which supply the diaphragm.

name: Left renal artery
note: The renal arteries are paired arteries that supply the kidneys with blood.

name: Anterior branch of renal artery (left)
note: Before reaching the hilus of the kidney, each artery divides into four or five branches.

name: Inferior suprarenal artery (left)
note: The inferior suprarenal artery is a paired artery that supplies the adrenal gland.

name: Posterior branch of renal artery (left)
note: Before reaching the hilus of the kidney, each artery divides into four or five branches.

name: Lumbar arteries (left)

name: Posterior branch of renal artery (right)

name: Superior mesenteric artery
note: In human anatomy, the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) arises from the anterior surface of the abdominal aorta, just inferior to the origin of the celiac trunk, and supplies blood to the intestine from the lower part of the duodenum through two-thirds of the transverse colon, as well as the pancreas.

name: Appendicular artery
note: The appendicular artery, also known as appendiceal artery, commonly arises from the terminal branch of the ileocolic artery, or less commonly from the posterior cecal artery or an ileal artery.

name: Colic branch of ileocolic artery
note: The colic branch of ileocolic artery is a small artery in the abdomen.

name: Ileal branch of ileocolic artery
note: The ileal branch of ileocolic artery is a branch of the ileocolic artery.

name: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
note: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (the IPDA) is a branch of the superior mesenteric artery.

name: Middle colic artery
note: The middle colic artery is an artery of the abdomen.

name: Right colic artery
note: The right colic artery is an artery of the abdomen.

name: Aortic arch
note: The aortic arch, arch of the aorta, or transverse aortic arch (English:) is the part of the aorta between the ascending and descending aorta.

name: Brachiocephalic trunk
note: The brachiocephalic arterial trunk is an artery that arises from the aorta, it is located in the superior mediastinum and carries oxygenated blood to the right upper limb, the head and the neck.

name: Common iliac artery (left)
note: The common iliac artery is a large artery of the abdomen paired on each side.

name: External iliac artery (left)
note: The external iliac arteries are two major arteries which bifurcate off the common iliac arteries anterior to the sacroiliac joint of the pelvis.

name: Inferior epigastric artery (left)
note: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric artery refers to the artery that arises from the external iliac artery.

name: Internal iliac artery (left)
note: The internal iliac artery (formerly known as the hypogastric artery) is the main artery of the pelvis.

name: Anterior division of internal iliac artery (left)
Inferior gluteal artery (left)
note: The inferior gluteal artery (sciatic artery), the smaller of the two terminal branches of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery, is distributed chiefly to the buttock and back of the thigh.

name: Internal pudendal artery (left)
note: The internal pudendal artery is one of the three pudendal arteries that branches off the internal iliac artery.

name: Deep artery of penis (left)
note: The deep artery of the penis (artery to the corpus cavernosum), one of the terminal branches of the internal pudendal, arises from that vessel while it is situated between the two fasciæ of the urogenital diaphragm (deep perineal pouch).

name: Dorsal artery of penis (left)
note: The dorsal artery of the penis is an artery on the top surface of the penis.

name: Posterior division of internal iliac artery (left)
note: The arrangement of branches of the internal iliac artery is variable.

name: Iliolumbar artery (left)
note: The iliolumbar artery is the first branch of the posterior trunk of the internal iliac artery.

name: Lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery (left)
note: The lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery (ramus lumbalis) supplies the psoas major and quadratus lumborum, anastomoses with the last lumbar artery, and sends a small spinal branch through the intervertebral foramen between the last lumbar vertebra and the sacrum, into the vertebral canal to supply the cauda equina.

name: Superior gluteal artery (left)
note: The superior gluteal artery is the largest and final branch of the internal iliac artery.

name: Common iliac artery (right)
note: The common iliac artery is a large artery of the abdomen paired on each side.

name: External iliac artery (right)
note: The external iliac arteries are two major arteries which bifurcate off the common iliac arteries anterior to the sacroiliac joint of the pelvis.

name: Inferior epigastric artery (right)

name: Dorsal artery of penis (right)
note: The dorsal artery of the penis is an artery on the top surface of the penis.

name: Obturator artery (left)
note: The obturator artery is a branch of the internal iliac artery that passes antero-inferiorly (forwards and downwards) on the lateral wall of the pelvis, to the upper part of the obturator foramen, and, escaping from the pelvic cavity through the obturator canal, it divides into both an anterior and a posterior branch.

name: Obturator artery (right)
note: The obturator artery is a branch of the internal iliac artery that passes antero-inferiorly (forwards and downwards) on the lateral wall of the pelvis, to the upper part of the obturator foramen, and, escaping from the pelvic cavity through the obturator canal, it divides into both an anterior and a posterior branch.

name: Posterior division of internal iliac artery (right)

name: Median sacral artery

name: Ascending aorta
note: The ascending aorta (AAo) is a portion of the aorta commencing at the upper part of the base of the left ventricle, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the sternum.

name: Thoracic aorta
note: The (descending) thoracic aorta is a part of the aorta located in the thorax.

name: Posterior intercostal arteries (left)
note: The intercostal arteries are a group of arteries that supply the area between the ribs ("costae"), called the intercostal space.

name: Posterior intercostal arteries (right)
note: The intercostal arteries are a group of arteries that supply the area between the ribs ("costae"), called the intercostal space.

name: Subcostal artery (left)
note: The subcostal arteries, so named because they lie below the last ribs, constitute the lowest pair of branches derived from the thoracic aorta, and are in series with the intercostal arteries.

name: Subcostal artery (right)

name: Superior phrenic arteries

name: Anterior spinal artery (left)

name: Anterior spinal artery (right)

name: Anterior communicating artery

name: Posterior communicating artery (left)

name: Posterior communicating artery (right)

name: Femoral artery (left)

name: Deep femoral artery (left)
note: The deep artery of the thigh, (profunda femoris artery or deep femoral artery) is a large branch of the femoral artery.

name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery (left)
note: The lateral circumflex femoral artery, also known as the lateral femoral circumflex artery, or the external circumflex artery, is an artery in the upper thigh.

name: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery (left)

name: Popliteal artery (left)
note: The popliteal artery is a deeply placed continuation of the femoral artery opening in the distal portion of the adductor magnus muscle.

name: Anterior tibial artery (left)

name: Dorsalis pedis artery (left)

name: Dorsal digital arteries of foot (left)
note: The dorsal digital arteries of foot are small arteries which supply the toes.

name: Deep plantar artery (left)

name: Inferior medial genicular artery (left)

name: Middle genicular artery (left)

name: Left common carotid artery

name: External carotid artery (left)
note: The external carotid artery is a major artery of the head and neck.

name: Ascending pharyngeal artery (left)
note: The ascending pharyngeal artery is an artery in the neck that supplies the pharynx, developing from the proximal part of the embryonic second aortic arch.

name: Facial artery (left)

name: Submental artery (left)

name: Superior labial artery (left)
note: The superior labial artery (superior labial branch of facial artery) is larger and more egregious than the inferior labial artery.

name: Maxillary artery (left)

name: Buccal artery (left)
note: The buccal artery (buccinator artery) is a small artery in the head.

name: Descending palatine artery (left)

name: Greater palatine artery (left)

name: Middle meningeal artery (left)

name: Occipital artery (left)

name: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery (left)

name: Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment) (left)

name: Insular branches of middle cerebral artery (M2-segment) (left)

name: Lacrimal artery (left)
note: The lacrimal artery is an artery of the orbit around the eye.

name: Long posterior ciliary arteries (left)

name: Posterior ethmoidal artery (left)

name: Septal branches of posterior ethmoidal artery (left)
Supratrochlear artery (left)

name: Left subclavian artery
note: In human anatomy, the subclavian arteries are paired major arteries of the upper thorax, below the clavicle.

name: Axillary artery (left)

name: Brachial artery (left)
note: The brachial artery is the major blood vessel of the (upper) arm.

name: Deep brachial artery (left)
note: The deep artery of arm (also known as arteria profunda brachii and the deep brachial artery) is a large vessel which arises from the lateral and posterior part of the brachial artery, just below the lower border of the teres major.

name: Dorsal venous arch of foot (right)
note: The dorsal venous arch of the foot is a superficial vein that connects the small saphenous vein and the great saphenous vein.

name: Dorsal metatarsal veins (right)
note: The dorsal metatarsal veins are veins which drain the metatarsus of the foot.

name: Dorsal digital veins of foot (right)
note: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

name: Intercapitular veins of foot (right)
note: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

name: Hepatic portal vein
note: The portal vein or hepatic portal vein (HPV) is a blood vessel that carries blood from the gastrointestinal tract, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen to the liver.

name: Splenic vein
note: The splenic vein (formerly the lienal vein) is a blood vessel that drains blood from the spleen, the stomach fundus and part of the pancreas.

name: Inferior mesenteric vein
note: In human anatomy, the inferior mesenteric vein (IMV) is a blood vessel that drains blood from the large intestine.

name: Left gastro-omental vein
note: The left gastroepiploic vein (left gastro-omental vein) receives branches from the antero-superior and postero-inferior surfaces of the stomach and from the greater omentum; it runs from right to left along the greater curvature of the stomach and ends in the commencement of the splenic vein.

name: Middle colic vein
note: The middle colic vein drains the transverse colon.

name: Right colic vein
note: The right colic vein drains the ascending colon, and is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein.

name: Right gastro-omental vein
note: The right gastro-omental vein is a blood vessel that drains blood from the greater curvature and left part of the body of the stomach into the superior mesenteric vein.

name: Inferior vena cava (thoracic part)
note: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that carries the deoxygenated blood from the lower and middle body into the right atrium of the heart.

name: Hepatic veins
note: The hepatic veins are the veins that drain de-oxygenated blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.

name: Inferior vena cava (abdominal part)
note: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that carries the deoxygenated blood from the lower and middle body into the right atrium of the heart.

name: Common iliac vein (left)
note: In human anatomy, the common iliac veins are formed by the external iliac veins and internal iliac veins.

name: External iliac vein (left)
note: The external iliac veins are large veins that connect the femoral veins to the common iliac veins.

name: Inferior epigastric vein (left)
note: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric vein refers to the vein that drains into the external iliac vein and anastomoses from the superior epigastric vein.

name: Iliolumbar vein (left)
note: The iliolumbar vein is the vena comitans of the iliolumbar artery.

name: Internal iliac vein (left)
note: The internal iliac vein (hypogastric vein) begins near the upper part of the greater sciatic foramen, passes upward behind and slightly medial to the internal iliac artery and, at the brim of the pelvis, joins with the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

name: Inferior gluteal veins (left)
note: The inferior gluteal veins (sciatic veins), or venae comitantes of the inferior gluteal artery, begin on the upper part of the back of the thigh, where they anastomose with the medial femoral circumflex and first perforating veins.

name: Internal pudendal vein (left)
note: The internal pudendal veins (internal pudic veins) are a set of veins in the pelvis.

name: Lateral sacral veins (left)
note: The lateral sacral veins accompany the lateral sacral arteries on the anterior surface of the sacrum and end in the hypogastric vein.

name: Superior gluteal veins (left)
note: The superior gluteal veins (gluteal veins) are venæ comitantes of the superior gluteal artery; they receive tributaries from the buttock corresponding with the branches of the artery, and enter the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, above the piriformis, and frequently unite before ending in the hypogastric vein (internal iliac vein).

name: Common iliac vein (right)
note: In human anatomy, the common iliac veins are formed by the external iliac veins and internal iliac veins.

name: External iliac vein (right)
note: The external iliac veins are large veins that connect the femoral veins to the common iliac veins.

name: Inferior epigastric vein (right)

name: Iliolumbar vein (right)

name: Inferior gluteal veins (right)

name: Left renal vein
note: There is one vein per kidney, that divides into 4 divisions upon entering the kidney: -the anterior branch which receives blood from the anterior portion of the kidney and, -the posterior branch which receives blood from the posterior portion.

name: Lumbar veins (left)
note: The lumbar veins are veins running along the inside of the posterior abdominal wall.

name: Lumbar veins (right)
note: The lumbar veins are veins running along the inside of the posterior abdominal wall.

name: Right renal vein

name: Internal jugular vein (left)
note: The internal jugular vein is a paired jugular vein that collects blood from the brain and the superficial parts of the face and neck.

name: Common facial vein (left)
note: The facial vein usually unites with the anterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which crosses the external carotid artery and enters the internal jugular vein at a variable point below the hyoid bone.

name: Anterior division of retromandibular vein (left)
note: The retromandibular vein emerges from the confluence of several veins, in front of the ear, and reaches the facial vein.

name: Retromandibular vein (left)
note: The retromandibular vein (temporomaxillary vein, posterior facial vein) is a major vein of the face.

name: Maxillary veins (left)
note: The maxillary vein, or internal maxillary vein, is a vein of the head.

name: Superficial temporal veins (left)
note: The superficial temporal vein is a vein of the side of the head.

name: Facial vein (left)
note: The facial vein (or anterior facial vein) is a relatively large vein in the human face.

name: Angular vein (left)
note: The angular vein is a vein of the face.

name: Inferior labial veins (left)
note: The inferior labial veins drain the blood of the inferior part of the oral region to the facial vein, then to the common facial vein, then to the internal jugular vein.

name: Submental vein (left)

name: Superior labial vein (left)
note: The superior labial vein is the vein receiving blood from the upper lip.

name: Basilic vein (left)

name: Median cubital vein (left)

name: Median antebrachial vein (left)

name: Brachial veins (left)

name: Radial veins (left)

name: Deep venous palmar arch (left)
note: The deep palmar arch is accompanied by a pair of venae comitantes which constitute the deep palmar venous arch.

name: Ulnar veins (left)

name: Superficial venous palmar arch (left)
note: The superficial palmar arch is accompanied by a pair of venae comitantes which constitute the superficial palmar venous arch.

name: Palmar digital veins (left)
note: The palmar digital veins (or volar digital veins) on each finger are connected to the dorsal digital veins by oblique intercapitular veins.

name: Cephalic vein (left)
note: In human anatomy, the cephalic vein is a superficial vein in the arm.

name: Dorsal venous network of hand (left)

name: Azygos vein
note: The azygos vein is a vein running up the right side of the thoracic vertebral column draining itself towards the superior vena cava.

name: Hemi-azygos vein
note: The hemi-azygos vein (vena azygos minor inferior) is a vein running superiorly in the lower thoracic region, just to the left side of the vertebral column.

name: Left brachiocephalic vein
note: The left and right brachiocephalic veins (or innominate veins) are major veins in the upper chest, formed by the union of each corresponding internal jugular vein and subclavian vein.

name: Internal thoracic veins (left)

name: Musculophrenic veins (left)

name: Superior epigastric veins (left)

name: Medial geniculate body (right)

name: Thalamus (left)

name: Thalamus (right)

name: Posterior commissure

name: Stria medullaris thalami (right)

name: Amygdaloid body (right)

name: Septal nuclei

name: Caudate nucleus (right)

name: Putamen (right)

name: Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus (right)

name: Middle frontal gyrus (left)

The middle frontal gyrus, like the inferior frontal gyrus and the superior frontal gyrus, is more of a region in the frontal gyrus than a true gyrus.

name: Middle frontal gyrus (right)
note: The middle frontal gyrus makes up about one-third of the frontal lobe of the human brain. (A gyrus is one of the prominent "bumps" or "ridges" on the surface of the human brain.) The middle frontal gyrus, like the inferior frontal gyrus and the superior frontal gyrus, is more of a region in the frontal gyrus than a true gyrus.

name: Olfactory sulcus (right)

name: Precentral sulcus (inferior part)* (right)

name: Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus) (left)

name: Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus) (right)

name: Superior frontal gyrus (right)
note: The superior frontal gyrus (SFG) also marginal gyrus, makes up about one third of the frontal lobe of the human brain.

name: Superior frontal sulcus (right)
note: The superior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the superior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus.

name: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (left)

name: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (right)

name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (left)
note: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (right)

name: Central sulcus (left)
note: The central sulcus is a sulcus, or groove, in the cerebral cortex in the brains of vertebrates.

name: Central sulcus (right)

name: Circular sulcus of insula (left)
note: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

name: Circular sulcus of insula (right)
note: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

name: Collateral sulcus (left)
note: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

name: Collateral sulcus (right)
note: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

name: Parieto-occipital sulcus (left)
note: The parieto-occipital sulcus (also called the parieto-occipital fissure) is a deep sulcus in the cerebral cortex that marks the boundary between the cuneus and precuneus, and also between the parietal and occipital lobes.

name: Parieto-occipital sulcus (right)
note: The parieto-occipital sulcus (also called the parieto-occipital fissure) is a deep sulcus in the cerebral cortex that marks the boundary between the cuneus and precuneus, and also between the parietal and occipital lobes.

name: Subparietal sulcus (left)
note: The subparietal sulcus (Sulcus subparietalis) or suprasplenial sulcus is a sulcus, or crevice, on the medial surface of each cerebral hemisphere, above the splenium of the corpus callosum.

name: Subparietal sulcus (right)
note: The subparietal sulcus (Sulcus subparietalis) or suprasplenial sulcus is a sulcus, or crevice, on the medial surface of each cerebral hemisphere, above the splenium of the corpus callosum.

name: Lateral ventricle (right)
note: The lateral ventricles are the two largest ventricles of the brain and contain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: Postcentral sulcus (right)

name: Transverse temporal gyri (right)

name: Posterior horn of spinal cord
note: The posterior grey column (posterior cornu, dorsal horn, spinal dorsal horn, posterior horn, sensory horn[1]) of the spinal cord is one of the three grey columns of the spinal cord.

name: Anterior corticospinal tract
note: The anterior corticospinal tract (also called the ventral corticospinal tract, "Bundle of Turck", medial corticospinal tract, direct pyramidal tract, or anterior cerebrospinal fasciculus) is a small bundle of descending fibers that connect the cerebral cortex to the spinal cord.

name: Anterior fasciculus proprius
note: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts, are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

name: Lateral vestibulospinal tract
note: The lateral vestibulospinal tract is one of the descending spinal tracts of the ventromedial funiculus.

name: Medial reticulospinal tract
note: The medial reticular formation and lateral reticular formation are two columns of nuclei with ill-defined boundaries that send projections through the medulla and into the midbrain.

name: Medial vestibulospinal tract
note: The medial vestibulospinal tract is one of the descending spinal tracts of the ventromedial funiculus of the spinal cord.

name: Tectospinal tract
note: In humans, the tectospinal tract (or colliculospinal tract) is a nerve tract that coordinates head and eye movements.

name: Anterior spinothalamic tract
note: The anterior spinothalamic tract, (Latin: tractus spinothalamicus anterior) or ventral spinothalamic fasciculus situated in the marginal part of the anterior funiculus and intermingled more or less with the vestibulospinal tract, is derived from cells in the posterior column or intermediate gray matter of the opposite side.

name: Lateral spinothalamic tract
note: The lateral spinothalamic tract (or lateral spinothalamic fasciculus), is a bundle of afferent nerve fibers ascending through the white matter of the spinal cord, in the spinothalamic tract, carrying sensory information to the brain.

name: Spinotectal tract
note: The spinotectal tract (spinomesencephalic tract, spinotectal fasciculus, spino-quadrigeminal system of Mott) arises in the spinothalamic tract and terminates in the inferior and superior colliculi.It is situated ventral to the lateral spinothalamic tract, but its fibers are more or less intermingled with it.

name: Anterior spinocerebellar tract
note: The ventral spinocerebellar tract (or anterior spinocerebellar tract) conveys proprioceptive information from the body to the cerebellum.

name: Lateral corticospinal tract
note: The lateral corticospinal tract (also called the crossed pyramidal tract or lateral cerebrospinal fasciculus) is the largest part of the corticospinal tract.

name: Lateral fasciculus proprius
note: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts, are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

name: Lateral reticulospinal tract
note: The medial reticular formation and lateral reticular formation are two columns of nuclei with ill-defined boundaries that send projections through the medulla and into the midbrain.

name: Posterior spinocerebellar tract
note: The spinocerebellar tract is a nerve tract originating in the spinal cord and terminating in the same side (ipsilateral) of the cerebellum.

name: Rubrospinal tract
note: The rubrospinal tract is a part of the nervous system.

name: Cuneate fasciculus
note: The cuneate fasciculus is triangular on transverse section, and lies between the gracile fasciculus and the posterior column, its base corresponding with the surface of the spinal cord.

name: Gracile fasciculus
note: The gracile fasciculus carries sensory information from the lower half of the body entering the spinal cord at the lumbar level.

name: Posterior fasciculus proprius
note: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts,[1] are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

name: Posterolateral tract
note: The posterolateral tract (fasciculus of Lissauer, Lissauer's tract, tract of Lissauer, dorsolateral fasciculus, dorsolateral tract, zone of Lissauer) is a small strand situated in relation to the tip of the posterior column close to the entrance of the posterior nerve roots.

name: White matter of spinal cord
note: In cross-section, the peripheral region of the cord contains neuronal white matter tracts containing sensory and motor axons.

name: Sympathetic nerves (left)
note: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is one of two divisions of the autonomic nervous system, along with the parasympathetic nervous system.

name: Sympathetic nerves (right)
note: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is one of two divisions of the autonomic nervous system, along with the parasympathetic nervous system.

name: Sympathetic trunk (left)
note: The sympathetic trunks (sympathetic chain, gangliated cord) are a paired bundle of nerve fibers that run from the base of the skull to the coccyx.

name: Ganglia of sympathetic trunk (left)
note: The sympathetic ganglia, or paravertebral ganglia are autonomic ganglia, of the sympathetic nervous system.

name: Sympathetic trunk (right)
note: The sympathetic trunks (sympathetic chain, gangliated cord) are a paired bundle of nerve fibers that run from the base of the skull to the coccyx.

name: Ganglia of sympathetic trunk (right)
note: The sympathetic ganglia, or paravertebral ganglia are autonomic ganglia, of the sympathetic nervous system.

name: Abducens nerve (VI) (left)
note: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze.

name: Abducens nerve (VI) (right)
note: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze.

name: Facial nerve (VII) (left)
note: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII.

name: Chorda tympani (left)
note: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

name: Facial nerve (VII) (right)
note: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII.

name: Chorda tympani (right)
note: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (left)
note: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information.

name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (right)
note: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information.

name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (left)
note: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve.

name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (right)
note: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve.

name: Oculomotor nerve (III) (left)
note: The oculomotor nerve is the third cranial nerve (CN III).

name: Oculomotor nerve (III) (right)
note: The oculomotor nerve is the third cranial nerve (CN III).

name: Olfactory nerve (I) (left)
note: The olfactory nerve is typically considered the first cranial nerve, or simply CN I, that contains sensory nerve fibers relating to the sense of smell.

name: Olfactory nerve (I) (right)
note: The olfactory nerve is typically considered the first cranial nerve, or simply CN I, that contains sensory nerve fibers relating to the sense of smell.

name: Optic nerve (II) (left)
note: The optic nerve, also known as cranial nerve II, or simply as CN II, is a paired cranial nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.

name: Optic nerve (II) (right)
note: The optic nerve, also known as cranial nerve II, or simply as CN II, is a paired cranial nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.

name: Trigeminal nerve (V) (left)
note: The trigeminal nerve (the fifth cranial nerve, or simply CN V) is a nerve responsible for sensation in the face and motor functions such as biting and chewing; it is the most complex of the cranial nerves.

name: Maxillary nerve (left)
note: The maxillary nerve (V2) is one of the three branches or divisions of the trigeminal nerve, the fifth (CN V) cranial nerve.

name: Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve (left)
note: MENINGEAL BRANCH OF THE MANDIBULAR NERVE (to be verified) The meningeal (recurrent) branch of the mandibular nerve (nervus spinosus) is a branch of the mandibular nerve that supplies the dura mater.

name: Motor root of trigeminal nerve (left)
note: The trigeminal motor nucleus contains motor neurons that innervate muscles of the first branchial arch, namely the muscles of mastication, the tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, and anterior belly of the digastric.

name: Ophthalmic nerve (left)
note: The ophthalmic nerve (V1) is a sensory nerve of the face.

name: Sensory root of trigeminal nerve (left)
note: The principal sensory nucleus of trigeminal nerve (or chief sensory nucleus of V, main trigeminal sensory nucleus) is a group of second-order neurons which have cell bodies in the caudal pons.

name: Trigeminal nerve (V) (right)
note: The trigeminal nerve (the fifth cranial nerve, or simply CN V) is a nerve responsible for sensation in the face and motor functions such as biting and chewing; it is the most complex of the cranial nerves.

name: Maxillary nerve (right)
note: The maxillary nerve (V2) is one of the three branches or divisions of the trigeminal nerve, the fifth (CN V) cranial nerve.

name: Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve (right)
note: MENINGEAL BRANCH OF THE MANDIBULAR NERVE (to be verified) The meningeal (recurrent) branch of the mandibular nerve (nervus spinosus) is a branch of the mandibular nerve that supplies the dura mater.

name: Motor root of trigeminal nerve (right)
note: The trigeminal motor nucleus contains motor neurons that innervate muscles of the first branchial arch, namely the muscles of mastication, the tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, and anterior belly of the digastric.

name: Ophthalmic nerve (right)
note: The ophthalmic nerve (V1) is a sensory nerve of the face.

name: Sensory root of trigeminal nerve (right)
note: The principal sensory nucleus of trigeminal nerve (or chief sensory nucleus of V, main trigeminal sensory nucleus) is a group of second-order neurons which have cell bodies in the caudal pons.

name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (left)
note: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

name: Buccal nerve (left)
note: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face.

name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (right)
note: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

name: Buccal nerve (right)
note: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face.

name: Posterior division of mandibular nerve (left)
note: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

name: Inferior alveolar nerve (left)
note: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve.

name: Mental nerve (left)
note: Mental nerve is a sensory nerve which provides sensation to the front of the chin and lower lip as well as the labial gingivae of the mandibular anterior teeth and the premolars.

name: Lingual nerve (left)
note: The lingual nerve carries sensory innervation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

name: Posterior division of mandibular nerve (right)
note: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

name: Inferior alveolar nerve (right)
note: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve.

name: Mental nerve (right)
note: Mental nerve is a sensory nerve which provides sensation to the front of the chin and lower lip as well as the labial gingivae of the mandibular anterior teeth and the premolars.

name: Lingual nerve (right)
note: The lingual nerve carries sensory innervation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

name: Trochlear nerve (IV) (left)
note: The trochlear nerve , also called the fourth cranial nerve or CN IV, is a motor nerve (a somatic efferent nerve) that innervates just one muscle: the superior oblique muscle of the eye, which operates through the pulley-like trochlea.

name: Trochlear nerve (IV) (right)
note: The trochlear nerve , also called the fourth cranial nerve or CN IV, is a motor nerve (a somatic efferent nerve) that innervates just one muscle: the superior oblique muscle of the eye, which operates through the pulley-like trochlea.

name: Vagus nerve (X) (left)
note: The vagus nerve, historically cited as the pneumogastric nerve, is the tenth cranial nerve or CN X, and interfaces with the parasympathetic control of the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.

name: Vagus nerve (X) (right)
note: The vagus nerve, historically cited as the pneumogastric nerve, is the tenth cranial nerve or CN X, and interfaces with the parasympathetic control of the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.

name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII) (left)
note: The vestibulocochlear nerve (auditory vestibular nerve), known as the eighth cranial nerve, transmits sound and equilibrium (balance) information from the inner ear to the brain.

name: Cochlear nerve (left)
note: The cochlear nerve (also auditory nerve or acoustic nerve) is one of two parts of the vestibulocochlear nerve, a cranial nerve present in amniotes, the other part being the vestibular nerve.

name: Vestibular nerve (left)
note: The vestibular nerve is one of the two branches of the vestibulocochlear nerve (the cochlear nerve being the other).

name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII) (right)
note: The vestibulocochlear nerve (auditory vestibular nerve), known as the eighth cranial nerve, transmits sound and equilibrium (balance) information from the inner ear to the brain.

name: Cochlear nerve
note: The cochlear nerve (also auditory nerve or acoustic nerve) is one of two parts of the vestibulocochlear nerve, a cranial nerve present in amniotes, the other part being the vestibular nerve.

name: Vestibular nerve (right)
note: The vestibular nerve is one of the two branches of the vestibulocochlear nerve (the cochlear nerve being the other).

name: Spinal ganglion (left)
note: A dorsal root ganglion (or spinal ganglion; also known as a posterior root ganglion) is a cluster of neurons (a ganglion) in a dorsal root of a spinal nerve.

name: Spinal ganglion (right)
note: A dorsal root ganglion (or spinal ganglion; also known as a posterior root ganglion) is a cluster of neurons (a ganglion) in a dorsal root of a spinal nerve.

name: Cauda equina
note: The cauda equina (from Latin horse's tail) is a bundle of spinal nerves and spinal nerve rootlets, consisting of the second through fifth lumbar nerve pairs, the first through fifth sacral nerve pairs, and the coccygeal nerve, all of which arise from the lumbar enlargement and the conus medullaris of the spinal cord.

name: Anterior root of spinal nerve (left)
note: The anterior root of spinal nerve, or ventral root, or motor root, is the efferent motor root of a spinal nerve.

name: Anterior root of spinal nerve (right)
note: The anterior root of spinal nerve, or ventral root, or motor root, is the efferent motor root of a spinal nerve.

name: Lateral pectoral nerve (left)
note: The lateral pectoral nerve (also known as the lateral anterior thoracic nerve) arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, and through it from the C5-7.

name: Lateral pectoral nerve (right)
note: The lateral pectoral nerve (also known as the lateral anterior thoracic nerve) arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, and through it from the C5-7.

name: Musculocutaneous nerve (left)
note: The musculocutaneous nerve arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, opposite the lower border of the pectoralis major, its fibers being derived from C5, C6 and C7.

name: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
note: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (or lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm) (branch of musculocutaneous nerve, also sometimes spelled "antebrachial") passes behind the cephalic vein, and divides, opposite the elbow-joint, into a volar and a dorsal branch.

name: Musculocutaneous nerve (right)
note: The musculocutaneous nerve arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, opposite the lower border of the pectoralis major, its fibers being derived from C5, C6 and C7.

name: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
note: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (or lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm) (branch of musculocutaneous nerve, also sometimes spelled "antebrachial") passes behind the cephalic vein, and divides, opposite the elbow-joint, into a volar and a dorsal branch.

name: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
note: The medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve) branches from the medial cord of the brachial plexus.

name: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
latin: Ramus anterior nervi cutanei medialis antebrachii
note: The volar branch (ramus volaris; anterior branch), the larger, passes usually in front of, but occasionally behind, the vena mediana cubiti (median basilic vein).

name: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
latin: Ramus posterior nervi cutanei medialis antebrachii
note: The ulnar branch (ramus ulnaris; posterior branch) passes obliquely downward on the medial side of the basilic vein, in front of the medial epicondyle of the humerus, to the back of the forearm, and descends on its ulnar side as far as the wrist, distributing filaments to the skin.

name: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
note: The medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve) branches from the medial cord of the brachial plexus.

name: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)

note: The volar branch (ramus volaris; anterior branch), the larger, passes usually in front of, but occasionally behind, the vena mediana cubiti (median basilic vein).

name: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)

note: The ulnar branch (ramus ulnaris; posterior branch) passes obliquely downward on the medial side of the basilic vein, in front of the medial epicondyle of the humerus, to the back of the forearm, and descends on its ulnar side as far as the wrist, distributing filaments to the skin.

name: Medial brachial cutaneous nerve (left)
note: The medial brachial cutaneous nerve (lesser internal cutaneous nerve; medial cutaneous nerve of arm) is distributed to the skin on the medial brachial side of the arm.

name: Medial brachial cutaneous nerve (right)

name: Superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve (right)

note: The paired submandibular glands (historically known as submaxillary glands) are major salivary glands located beneath the floor of the mouth.

name: Soft palate
note: The soft palate (also known as the velum, palatal velum, or muscular palate) is, in mammals, the soft tissue constituting the back of the roof of the mouth.

name: Tongue
note: The tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth of a typical tetrapod.

name: Uvula of palate
note: The palatine uvula, usually referred to as simply the uvula, is a conic projection from the back edge of the middle of the soft palate, composed of connective tissue containing a number of racemose glands, and some muscular fibers.

name: Pancreas
note: The pancreas is an organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.

name: Accessory pancreatic duct
note: Most people have just one pancreatic duct.

name: Pancreatic duct
note: The pancreatic duct, or duct of Wirsung (also, the major pancreatic duct due to the existence of an accessory pancreatic duct), is a duct joining the pancreas to the common bile duct.

name: Laryngopharynx
note: The laryngopharynx, (Latin: pars laryngea pharyngis), also known as hypopharynx, is the caudal part of the pharynx; it is the part of the throat that connects to the esophagus.

name: Nasopharynx
note: The upper portion of the pharynx, the nasopharynx, extends from the base of the skull to the upper surface of the soft palate.

name: Oropharynx
note: The oropharynx lies behind the oral cavity, extending from the uvula to the level of the hyoid bone.

name: Adenohypophysis
note: A major organ of the endocrine system, the anterior pituitary (also called the adenohypophysis or pars anterior) is the glandular, anterior lobe that together with the posterior lobe (posterior pituitary, or the neurohypophysis) makes up the pituitary gland (hypophysis).

name: Neurohypophysis
note: The posterior pituitary (or neurohypophysis) is the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland which is part of the endocrine system.

name: Inferior parathyroid gland (left)
note: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

name: Inferior parathyroid gland (right)
note: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

name: Superior parathyroid gland (left)
note: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

name: Superior parathyroid gland (right)
note: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

name: Pineal gland
note: The pineal gland, conarium, or epiphysis cerebri, is a small endocrine gland in the brain of most vertebrates.

name: Suprarenal gland (left)
note: The suprarenal glands (also known as adrenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including suprarenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.

name: Suprarenal gland (right)
note: The suprarenal glands (also known as adrenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including suprarenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.

name: Thyroid gland
note: The thyroid, or thyroid gland, is an endocrine gland in vertebrates.

name: Corpus cavernosum of penis
note: A corpus cavernosum penis (singular) (literally "cave-like body" of the penis, plural corpora cavernosa) is one of a pair of sponge-like regions of erectile tissue, which contain most of the blood in the penis during an erection.

name: Corpus spongiosum of penis
note: The corpus spongiosum is the mass of spongy tissue surrounding the male urethra within the penis.

name: Glans penis
note: The glans penis, commonly referred to as the glans, is a structure at the distal end of the penis in male mammals.

name: Ductus deferens (left)
note: The vas deferens, or ductus deferens, is part of the male reproductive system of many vertebrates.

name: Ductus deferens (right)
note: The vas deferens, or ductus deferens, is part of the male reproductive system of many vertebrates.

name: Ejaculatory duct (left)
note: The ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in male anatomy.

name: Ejaculatory duct (right)
note: The ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in male anatomy.

name: Epididymis (left)
note: The epididymis (; plural: epididymides or) is a tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

name: Epididymis (right)
note: The epididymis (; plural: epididymides or) is a tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

name: Prostate
note: The prostate is both an accessory gland of the male reproductive system and a muscle-driven mechanical switch between urination and ejaculation.

name: Seminal gland (left)
note: The seminal vesicles (also called vesicular glands, or seminal glands) are a pair of two convoluted tubular glands that lie behind the urinary bladder of some male mammals.

name: Seminal gland (right)
note: The seminal vesicles (also called vesicular glands, or seminal glands) are a pair of two convoluted tubular glands that lie behind the urinary bladder of some male mammals.

name: Testis (left)
note: Testicle or testis (plural testes) is the male reproductive gland or gonad in all animals, including humans.

name: Testis (right)
note: Testicle or testis (plural testes) is the male reproductive gland or gonad in all animals, including humans.

name: Epiglottis
note: The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped flap in the throat that prevents food from entering the windpipe and the lungs.

name: Inferior lobe of left lung
note: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

name: Superior lobe of left lung
note: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

name: Inferior lobe of right lung
note: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

name: Middle lobe of right lung
note: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

name: Superior lobe of right lung
note: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

name: Left main bronchus
note: A bronchus is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.

name: Left inferior lobar bronchus
note: For the inferior lobe that extends upwards until the fourth thoracic vertebra.

name: (Anteromedial basal segmental bronchus of left lung)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anteromed. pulmonis sinistri

name: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BVIII)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis ant. pulmonis sinistri (BVIII)
note: For the basal segment that touches the inferior part of the anterior border of the lung.

name: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BIX)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lat. pulmonis sinistri (BIX)
note: For the basal segment, in intermediary situation between the anterior and posterior basal segments.

name: Medial basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BVII)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis med. pulmonis sinistri (BVII)
note: For the medial basal segment that does not reach the external surface of the lung.

name: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BX)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis sinistri (BX)
note: For the segment located beneath the superior segment of the inferior lobe.

name: Superior segmental bronchus of left lung (BVI)
note: For the apical segment, in postero-superior situation in the inferior lobe.

name: Anterior segmental bronchus of left lung (BIII)
note: For the anterior segment taht extends rearwards to approximately the midaxillary line.

name: Apicoposterior segmental bronchus of left lung (BI+BII)
note: For the segment located in the superior and posterior part of the superior lobe of left lung.

name: Inferior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (BV)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis lingularis inf. pulmonis sinistri (BV)
note: For the lower segment of the superior lobe of left lung, mainly anterior.

name: Superior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (BIV)
latin: Bronchus segm. lingularis sup. pulmonis sinistri (BIV)
note: For the second lower segment of the left superior lobe, reaching rearward the limit of the inferior lobe.

name: Right main bronchus
note: A bronchus is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.

name: Intermediate bronchus (right)
note: The bronchus intermedius runs distal to the right upper lobe bifurcation and follows the trajectory of the right main bronchus.

name: Lateral segmental bronchus of right lung (BIV)
note: For the lateral segment, located dorsally to the middle lobe.

name: Medial segmental bronchus of right lung (BV)
note: For the medial segment, located medially in the middle lobe.

name: Right inferior lobar bronchus
note: For the right inferior lobe, going back up rearward until the fourth rib.

name: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BVIII)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis ant. pulmonis dextri (BVIII)
note: For the anterior segment, corner-shaped, of the inferior lobe.

name: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BIX)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lat. pulmonis dextri (BIX)
note: For the small lateral segment, located between the anterior and the posterior segments.

name: Medial basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BVII)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis med. pulmonis dextri (BVII)
note: For the medial segment of the inferior lobe, that does not reach the external surface of this lobe.

name: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BX)
latin: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis dextri (BX)
note: For the posterior segment that extends rearwards until the vertebral column.

name: Superior segmental bronchus of right lung (BVI)
note: For the apical segment, in contact only with the superior lobe.

name: Right superior lobar bronchus
note: The eparterial bronchus (right superior lobar bronchus) is a branch of the right main bronchus given off about 2.5 cm from the bifurcation of the trachea.

name: Anterior segmental bronchus of right lung (BIII)
note: For the anterior segment, that extends rearwards until approximately the midaxillary line.

name: Apical segmental bronchus of right lung (BI)
note: For the apical segment of right lung, that extends until the third rib bellow.

name: Posterior segmental bronchus of right lung (BII)
note: For the posterior segment, that extends approximately until the midaxillary line.

name: Trachea
note: The trachea, also known as the windpipe, is a cartilaginous tube that connects the larynx to the bronchi of the lungs, allowing the passage of air, and so is present in almost all air-breathing animals with lungs.

name: Pleura
note: The pulmonary pleurae (sing. pleura) are the two opposing layers of serous membrane overlying the lungs and the inside of the surrounding chest walls.

name: Kidney (left)
note: The kidneys are two reddish-brown bean-shaped organs found in vertebrates.

name: Kidney (right)
note: The kidneys are two reddish-brown bean-shaped organs found in vertebrates.

name: Renal pelvis (left)
note: The renal pelvis or pelvis of the kidney is the funnel-like dilated part of the ureter in the kidney.

name: Renal pelvis (right)
note: The renal pelvis or pelvis of the kidney is the funnel-like dilated part of the ureter in the kidney.

name: Ureter (left)
note: The ureters are tubes made of smooth muscle that propel urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.

name: Ureter (right)
note: The ureters are tubes made of smooth muscle that propel urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.

name: Urethra
note: The urethra (from Greek οὐρήθρα – ourḗthrā) is a tube that connects the urinary bladder to the urinary meatus for the removal of urine from the body of both females and males.

name: Urinary bladder
note: The urinary bladder, or simply bladder, is a hollow muscular organ in humans and other vertebrates that stores urine from the kidneys before disposal by urination.

name: Inferior diaphragmatic nodes
note: On the inferior surface of diaphragm, near the aortic hiatus.

name: Inferior epigastric nodes (left)
note: Three or four lymph nodes along the inferior epigastric artery for its territory.

name: Inferior epigastric nodes (right)
note: Three or four lymph nodes along the inferior epigastric artery for its territory.

name: Lateral aortic nodes
note: They are located on the left side of the abdominal aorta.

name: Pre-aortic nodes
note: The preaortic lymph nodes lie in front of the aorta, and may be divided into celiac lymph nodes, superior mesenteric lymph nodes, and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes groups, arranged around the origins of the corresponding arteries.

name: Retro-aortic nodes
note: The retroaortic lymph nodes (or postaortic lymph nodes) are placed below the cisterna chyli, on the bodies of the third and fourth lumbar vertebrae.

name: Lateral caval nodes
note: The lateral caval nodes are located on the right of the inferior vena cava.

name: Precaval nodes
note: They are located in front of the inferior vena cava.

name: Retrocaval nodes
note: The retrocaval nodes are located behind the inferior vena cava.

name: Coeliac nodes
note: The coeliac nodes are located around the coeliac trunk and are the second filtration relay of the stomach, the duodenum, the liver, the gallbladder, the pancreas and the spleen.

name: Cystic node
note: Big lympatic node next to the gallbladder.

name: Left colic nodes
note: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

name: Sigmoid nodes
note: Located along the sigmoid artery, for the sigmoid colon and the contiguous colic segment.

name: Intermediate lumbar nodes
note: Between the aorta and the inferior vena cava.

name: Superior pancreaticoduodenal nodes
note: Superior part of the pancreaticoduodenal nodes.

name: (Retropyloric nodes)
note: On the dorsal side of the pyloric part of the stomach.

name: (Subpyloric nodes)
note: On the caudal side of the pyloric part of the stomach.

name: Right gastric nodes
note: On the lesser curvature of stomach, they follow the path of the left/right gastric arteries. they drain the stomach and evacuate in the coeliac nodes.

name: Right gastro-omental nodes
note: The right and left gastro-omental nodes are located on the great curvature of stomach on the path of the left/right gastro-omental arteries.

name: Splenic nodes
note: The splenic lymph nodes are found at the splenic hilum and in relation to the tail of the pancreas (pancreaticolienal lymph nodes).

name: Appendicular nodes
note: The appendicular nodes are located along the appendicular artery.

name: Central superior mesenteric nodes
note: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located at the trunk of the superior mesenteric artery.

name: Ileocolic nodes
note: The ileocolic nodes are located along the ileocolic artery.

name: Juxta-intestinal mesenteric nodes
note: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located very close to the small intestine.

name: Middle colic nodes
note: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

name: Paracolic superior mesenteric nodes
note: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located next to the colon.

name: Precaecal nodes
note: The precaecal nodes are located along the anterior caecal artery.

name: Retrocaecal nodes
note: The retrocaecal are located along the posterior caecal artery.

name: Right colic nodes
note: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

name: Bucinator node (left)
note: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth.

name: Bucinator node (right)
note: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth.

name: Mandibular node (left)
note: the mandibular node is located on the external side of the mandible.

name: Mandibular node (right)
note: the mandibular node is located on the external side of the mandible.

name: Nasolabial node (left)
note: The nasolabial lymph node is a facial node found near the nose and upper lip.

name: Nasolabial node (right)
note: The nasolabial lymph node is a facial node found near the nose and upper lip.

name: Mastoid nodes (left)
note: The mastoid lymph nodes (retroauricular lymph nodes or posterior auricular glands) are a small group of lymph nodes, usually two in number, located just beneath the ear, on the mastoid insertion of the sternocleidomastoideus muscle, beneath the posterior auricular muscle.

name: Mastoid nodes (right)
note: The mastoid lymph nodes (retroauricular lymph nodes or posterior auricular glands) are a small group of lymph nodes, usually two in number, located just beneath the ear, on the mastoid insertion of the sternocleidomastoideus muscle, beneath the posterior auricular muscle.

name: Occipital nodes (left)
note: The occipital lymph nodes, one to three in number, are located on the back of the head close to the margin of the trapezius and resting on the insertion of the semispinalis capitis.

name: Occipital nodes (right)
note: The occipital lymph nodes, one to three in number, are located on the back of the head close to the margin of the trapezius and resting on the insertion of the semispinalis capitis.

name: Superficial popliteal nodes (left)
note: The superficial popliteal nodes are located at the proximal extremity of the lesser saphenous vein and drain the lymph of the lateral border of the foot and of the leg.

name: Superficial popliteal nodes (right)
note: The superficial popliteal nodes are located at the proximal extremity of the lesser saphenous vein and drain the lymph of the lateral border of the foot and of the leg.

name: Paratracheal cervical nodes
note: The right and left paratracheal nodes (or paratracheal chains) are groups of lymph nodes located laterally to the trachea; unlike the pretracheal nodes that are located in front of it.

name: Pretracheal nodes (left)
note: The pretracheal lymph nodes are lymph nodes located anterior to the trachea in the neck.

name: Pretracheal nodes (right)
note: The pretracheal lymph nodes are lymph nodes located anterior to the trachea in the neck.

name: Thyroid nodes (left)
note: The thyroid lymph nodes are deep anterior cervical lymph nodes found near the thyroid gland on the neck.

name: Thyroid nodes (right)
note: The thyroid lymph nodes are deep anterior cervical lymph nodes found near the thyroid gland on the neck.

name: Jugulodigastric node (left)
note: The jugulodigastric lymph nodes are large lymph nodes of the neck.

name: Jugulodigastric node (right)
note: The jugulodigastric lymph nodes are large lymph nodes of the neck.

name: Retropharyngeal nodes (left)
note: The retropharyngeal lymph nodes, from one to three in number, lie in the buccopharyngeal fascia, behind the upper part of the pharynx and in front of the arch of the atlas, being separated, however, from the latter by the Longus capitis.

name: Retropharyngeal nodes (right)
note: The retropharyngeal lymph nodes, from one to three in number, lie in the buccopharyngeal fascia, behind the upper part of the pharynx and in front of the arch of the atlas, being separated, however, from the latter by the Longus capitis.

name: Submandibular nodes (left)
note: The submandibular lymph nodes (submaxillary glands in older texts), three to six in number, are lymph nodes beneath the body of the mandible in the submandibular triangle, and rest on the superficial surface of the submandibular gland.

name: Submandibular nodes (right)
note: The submandibular lymph nodes (submaxillary glands in older texts), three to six in number, are lymph nodes beneath the body of the mandible in the submandibular triangle, and rest on the superficial surface of the submandibular gland.

name: Submental nodes (left)
note: The submental glands (or suprahyoid) are situated between the anterior bellies of the digastric muscle and the hyoid bone.

name: Submental nodes (right)
note: The submental glands (or suprahyoid) are situated between the anterior bellies of the digastric muscle and the hyoid bone.

name: Supraclavicular nodes (left)
note: Supraclavicular lymph nodes are lymph nodes found above the clavicle, that can be felt in the supraclavicular fossa.

name: Supraclavicular nodes (right)
note: Supraclavicular lymph nodes are lymph nodes found above the clavicle, that can be felt in the supraclavicular fossa.

name: Anterior axillary nodes (left)
note: An anterior or pectoral group consists of four or five glands along the lower border of the Pectoralis minor, in relation with the lateral thoracic artery.

name: Anterior axillary nodes (right)
note: An anterior or pectoral group consists of four or five glands along the lower border of the Pectoralis minor, in relation with the lateral thoracic artery.

name: Apical axillary nodes (left)
note: An apical (or medial or subclavicular) group of six to twelve glands is situated partly posterior to the upper portion of the Pectoralis minor and partly above the upper border of this muscle.

name: Apical axillary nodes (right)
note: An apical (or medial or subclavicular) group of six to twelve glands is situated partly posterior to the upper portion of the Pectoralis minor and partly above the upper border of this muscle.

name: Central axillary nodes (left)
note: A central or intermediate group of three or four large glands is imbedded in the adipose tissue near the base of the axilla.

name: Central axillary nodes (right)
note: A central or intermediate group of three or four large glands is imbedded in the adipose tissue near the base of the axilla.

name: Lateral axillary nodes (left)
note: A brachial lymph nodes (or lateral group) are group of four to six lymph nodes which lies in relation to the medial and posterior aspects of the axillary vein; the afferents of these glands drain the whole arm with the exception of that portion whose vessels accompany the cephalic vein.

name: Lateral axillary nodes (right)
note: A brachial lymph nodes (or lateral group) are group of four to six lymph nodes which lies in relation to the medial and posterior aspects of the axillary vein; the afferents of these glands drain the whole arm with the exception of that portion whose vessels accompany the cephalic vein.

name: Posterior axillary nodes (left)
note: A posterior or subscapular group of six or seven glands is placed along the lower margin of the posterior wall of the axilla in the course of the subscapular artery.

name: Posterior axillary nodes (right)
note: A posterior or subscapular group of six or seven glands is placed along the lower margin of the posterior wall of the axilla in the course of the subscapular artery.

name: Cubital nodes (left)
note: One or two lymph nodes along the brachial artery inside the cubital fossa.

name: Supratrochlear nodes (left)
note: One or two supratrochlear lymph nodes are placed above the medial epicondyle of the humerus, medial to the basilic vein.

name: Cubital nodes (right)
note: One or two lymph nodes along the brachial artery inside the cubital fossa.

name: Supratrochlear nodes (right)
note: One or two supratrochlear lymph nodes are placed above the medial epicondyle of the humerus, medial to the basilic vein.

name: Infraclavicular nodes (left)
note: One or two deltopectoral lymph nodes (or infraclavicular nodes) are found beside the cephalic vein, between the pectoralis major and deltoideus, immediately below the clavicle.

name: Infraclavicular nodes (right)
note: One or two deltopectoral lymph nodes (or infraclavicular nodes) are found beside the cephalic vein, between the pectoralis major and deltoideus, immediately below the clavicle.

name: Interpectoral nodes (left)
note: The small interpectoral lymph nodes are located between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles.

name: Interpectoral nodes (right)
note: The small interpectoral lymph nodes are located between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles.

name: Intermediate common iliac nodes
note: Those of the common iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial common iliac nodes and the lateral common iliac nodes.

name: Lateral common iliac nodes
note: Those of the common iliac nodes located on the lateral side of the vascular axis.

name: Medial common iliac nodes
note: Those of the common iliac nodes located on the medial side of the vascular axis.

name: Subaortic nodes
note: Those of the common iliac nodes located beneath the aortic bifurcation, in front of the 4th lumbar vertebra (Vertebra T4).

name: Intermediate external iliac nodes (left)
note: Group of external iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial external iliac nodes and the lateral external iliac nodes.

name: Intermediate external iliac nodes (right)
note: Group of external iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial external iliac nodes and the lateral external iliac nodes.

name: Inferior gluteal nodes (left)
note: They are located along the inferior gluteal nodes for the prostate and the proximal part of the ureter.

name: Inferior gluteal nodes (right)
note: They are located along the inferior gluteal nodes for the prostate and the proximal part of the ureter.

name: Superior gluteal nodes (left)
note: Located along the superior gluteal artery for the wall of the pelvis.

name: Superior gluteal nodes (right)
note: Located along the superior gluteal artery for the wall of the pelvis.

name: Lateral sacral nodes (left)
note: They are located against the sacrum; for the prostate and the neck of uterus.

name: Lateral sacral nodes (right)
note: They are located against the sacrum; for the prostate and the neck of uterus.

name: Postvesical nodes
note: Those of the paravesical nodes located behind the urinary bladder.

name: Prevesical nodes
note: Those of the vesical nodes located between the urinary bladder and the pubic symphysis.

name: Brachiocephalic nodes
note: In front of the aortic arch and of its branches; along the brachiocephalic veins.

name: Juxta-oesophageal nodes
note: They are located next to the oesophagus but belong to the lungs.

name: Node of arch of azygos vein
Prepericardial nodes
note: Located between the sternum and the pericardium, the prepericardial nodes drain the sternum and the anterior part of the pericardium.

name: Intercostal nodes (left)
note: The intercostal lymph nodes (intercostal glands) occupy the posterior parts of the intercostal spaces, in relation to the intercostal vessels.

name: Intercostal nodes (right)
note: The intercostal lymph nodes (intercostal glands) occupy the posterior parts of the intercostal spaces, in relation to the intercostal vessels.

name: Parasternal nodes (left)
note: The parasternal lymph nodes (or sternal glands) are placed at the anterior ends of the intercostal spaces, by the side of the internal thoracic artery.

name: Parasternal nodes (right)
note: The parasternal lymph nodes (or sternal glands) are placed at the anterior ends of the intercostal spaces, by the side of the internal thoracic artery.

name: Prevertebral nodes
note: The prevertebral lymph nodes are located between the oesophagus and the vertebral column.

name: Superior diaphragmatic nodes
note: The superior diaphragmatic lymph nodes lie on the thoracic aspect of the diaphragm, and consist of three sets – anterior, middle, and posterior.

name: Intrapulmonary nodes
note: The Intrapulmonary nodes or Lymphatic Vessels of the Lungs originate in two plexuses, a superficial and a deep.

name: Palatine tonsil (left)
note: Palatine tonsils, commonly called the tonsils and occasionally called the faucial tonsils, are tonsils located on the left and right sides at the back of the throat, which can often be seen as flesh-colored, pinkish lumps.

name: Palatine tonsil (right)
note: Palatine tonsils, commonly called the tonsils and occasionally called the faucial tonsils, are tonsils located on the left and right sides at the back of the throat, which can often be seen as flesh-colored, pinkish lumps.

name: Spleen
note: The spleen is an organ found in all vertebrates.
